source.title: Layer-wise and Dimension-wise Locally Adaptive Federated Learning
source.authors: Belhal Karimi; Ping Li; Xiaoyun Li

record.tranche_reason: Compares federated adaptive methods with Fed-SGD and reports held-out image-classification accuracy, extending optimizer comparisons to federated training.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy for several federated algorithms. It does not report training error or test error gaps, random-label fitting, width sweeps, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons, large-batch comparisons, dropout effects, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The baseline algorithms independently compare adaptive federated optimization with local SGD using image-classification test accuracy. These results bear on V4 in a federated setting, although training performance is unreported. Comparisons involving the authors' proposed LAMB methods are method-performance results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that layer-wise adaptive Fed-LAMB and Mime-LAMB accelerate federated convergence and often improve test accuracy under IID and non-IID data. Their convergence analysis matches existing rates and gives linear speedup with client count.
record.recipe_differences: Federated training with client sampling, local updates, periodic aggregation, and layer-wise adaptive updates; compares several federated algorithms rather than the single-machine optimizer recipes in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and algorithm change test accuracy; Fed-AMS is below Fed-SGD on TinyImageNet, while Fed-LAMB has the highest reported accuracy on both Table 2 datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Fed-LAMB and Mime-LAMB improve accuracy and convergence relative to several federated baselines; their weight decay is additionally tuned.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-wise adaptation can improve the accuracy and communication efficiency of locally adaptive federated optimization.

record.problems: The displayed accuracy comparisons are from non-IID federated settings and do not report training performance or a train–test gap. Table 2 results are averaged over 3 runs; no significance tests are stated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
A controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected generalization comparison and the contribution of local connectivity; using both architectures does not establish these effects.
Training-performance comparisons; centralized and language benchmarks; broader-tuning ablations; recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching optimizers; word-level language models.
An isolated batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a batch-size penalty. Figure 6 changes several settings together.
Dropout ablations, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Adaptive-baseline-versus-Fed-SGD accuracy comparisons for MNIST MLP, MNIST CNN and Fashion-MNIST CNN under IID and non-IID allocation, with one and three local epochs. In particular, record the explicitly stated Adp-Fed advantage over Fed-SGD on non-IID Fashion-MNIST at round 50. Separate endpoint accuracy from convergence speed.
Adaptive-baseline-versus-Fed-SGD endpoint accuracy comparisons with 200 clients, full participation and batch size 64. These conditions differ from Table 2 and are not represented in the record.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 2 numbers match the supplied text. Results average three runs; the meaning of ± is unspecified and no significance tests are reported. Faster convergence and fixed-round accuracy do not isolate an eventual generalization difference. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Non-federated image and language benchmarks; equal or better training performance; broad hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large-batch versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Removing influential memorized examples and measuring the test-accuracy effect.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Federated training with Fed-SGD; test accuracy after 100 communication rounds.
rows.note: Reference comparator for the reported algorithm comparisons.
rows.check: Valid SGD reference; alone it cannot establish an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage. Table 2 explicitly reports accuracy after 100 rounds, despite the general reporting statement about best test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18

rows.note: Test accuracy is higher than the Fed-SGD comparator.
rows.check: Adp-Fed exceeds Fed-SGD by 0.82 percentage points, opposite to the disadvantage named in V4. Adp-Fed uses local SGD and server-side Adam, with both learning rates tuned.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated June 2022. Results average three runs; uncertainty type and training performance are unreported. Table 2 explicitly gives end-of-training accuracy despite the general best-test-accuracy reporting statement.

statements.correction: Fed-AMS: local AMSGrad with shared second-moment information; Adp-Fed: local SGD with server-side Adam. Table 2, non-IID TinyImageNet, ResNet-18, 100 rounds: Fed-AMS 64.86±0.83%; Fed-SGD 67.58±0.21%.
statements.problem: The accuracy comparison is correct, but the conditions describe federated server adaptation; Fed-AMS uses adaptive client updates.
